entities.summary:
Þangbrandr was a missionary sent to Iceland by king of Norway Óláfr Tryggvason to convert the inhabitants to Christianity.

Þangbrandr, a Norwegian Christian missionary, arrived in Iceland in the late 10th century and played a pivotal role in the conversion of the Icelandic people to Christianity.

The Icelandic Saga of Þangbrandr recounts his journey, during which he encountered fierce resistance from the pagan Icelandic chieftains, but ultimately succeeded in converting many to Christianity.

Þangbrandr's mission was significant not only for Iceland but also for the broader Viking Age cultural landscape, as it marked one of the first attempts to Christianize the pagan Norse populations.

Snorri Sturluson described Þangbrandr as a 'Christian missionary from Norway' who 'preached the word of the Lord' in Iceland.
